open_obligations.title: A later FAIL does not supersede an earlier PASS (one effective evaluation, SECURITY.md limit 8)
open_obligations.target: Each world has exactly one effective evaluation: the newest completed evaluation under the current requirement, PASS or FAIL, selected by the proved kernel. A newer evaluation supersedes every older one, and a superseded evaluation never regains authority (roadmap Phase 1 item 5).
open_obligations.closure_required: M3 A6: give evaluations a monotonic per-world sequence; pass the whole ordered roster bound to the world's content to Worldline.Evaluation/Decide, which selects the newest completed evaluation under the current requirement whatever its verdict; write-ahead ERROR placeholder; Same(Expected_Epoch, Evidence_Epoch) in Decide; mark superseded records permanently non-speaking; remove the effective_evidence allowlist entry. Re-running until a PASS (OB-022) and rollback revival (OB-025) are separate obligations.
open_obligations.original_test: PASS then FAIL then prepare: refused. Revert the policy to the PASS's requirement: still refused. PASS, FAIL, newer PASS: allowed. A mutant restoring newest-PASS selection fails. Kernel fuzz oracle over PASS/FAIL sequences. The static audit fails if effective_evidence still compares verdicts.

open_obligations.title: A candidate can change the requirement that judges it and every later candidate (policy, verifier scope, protected set, examiners)
open_obligations.target: A candidate can never change the requirement that judges it or any later candidate: policy, verifier scope, protected set and examiners. The proved kernel refuses any such change (including a rewritten authoritative verifier, VERIFIER_MODIFIED_BY_CANDIDATE) in every promotion mode.
open_obligations.closure_required: M3 A1: in Candidate_Evaluation mode Decide requires Same(Current_Requirement, Resulting_Requirement), with Resulting_Requirement recomputed from the staging payload at prepare and at commit; pass context integrity as typed presence. The parts M3 v3 narrows stay open as separate obligations: non-primary roots (OB-017), symlinks and skipped directories in verifier scopes (OB-018), checkpoint returns (OB-024).
open_obligations.original_test: Candidates that do the work and also (a) loosen .worldline.json checks, (b) drop a protected pattern, (c) rewrite evaluator/exam.py are refused REQUIREMENT_CHANGED (with _freshness replaced by a pass-through double), while the 1.9.1 control is AUTHORIZED. A mutant removing the Same() conjunct fails the proof gate.

open_obligations.title: Candidate code can choose the verdict of a shared-process examiner (legacy one-identity checks; A5 strict variant declined)
open_obligations.target: A verdict that can authorize promotion comes from an examiner candidate code cannot reach or steer: determinate supervision (SUPERVISED, not stopped) and no candidate code in the examiner's process or identity (os._exit(0), unittest.SkipTest, monkeypatching can never yield an admitted PASS).
open_obligations.closure_required: M3 A5 (Supervised and not stopped, proved per call) plus the declined strict variant: add an Isolation observation (engine, agent, private worker, shared-process) to Classify; Admissible refuses shared-process External verdicts for required checks unless the PRIME policy marks the check data-only and the runtime enforces it (candidate tree mounted noexec, excluded from the examiner's import path). Migrate remaining legacy examiners to private-evaluator-v1 (OB-139). COSMOGONY owns only the policy default.
open_obligations.original_test: The INDETERMINATE probe is refused Incomplete_Unknown and a stopped supervisor Interrupted. R-A5-2 flips to not admitted for os._exit(0) and SkipTest. Kernel ABI rows for each isolation value; G3 L1 monotonicity holds. Add a named private-host roster case with zero skips.

open_obligations.title: Checks whose verifier is unbound or only partly bound are admitted with a warning (make test, -m pytest, sh -c, undeclared helpers, covered script operands)
open_obligations.target: Every check that can authorize promotion binds a verifier identity staged from PRIME covering everything it executes or imports, including the process that actually decides the verdict (argv program and interpreter script operand), or the policy is refused at load.
open_obligations.closure_required: M3 A2 (Unbound never Admissible, proved per call) plus: refuse at policy load any required check with no existing argv file or an undeclared top-level verifier, with a migration list naming each affected check; either refuse or bind the transitive import/source closure of a verifier; resolve the executed program and script operand and add a Classify fact 'examiner token bound' so Admissible refuses an operand under covers or unbound.
open_obligations.original_test: Policy with 'make test' and no verifiers is refused at load; with verifiers declared, a Makefile edit gets VERIFIER_MODIFIED_BY_CANDIDATE. A verifier importing helper.py: editing helper.py is detected or the policy is refused. R-A2-4 flips to not admitted with a named reason. The reviewer probe (roster_decision complete=True, NOT_COVERED) becomes a refusal.

open_obligations.title: For legacy checks, bytes the checks wrote are promoted as 'tested'
open_obligations.target: The promoted bytes are exactly the bytes examined before any check ran, immutable for the whole evaluation. Nothing a check, or candidate code it ran, wrote during checking can become PRIME.
open_obligations.closure_required: M3 A4: examinedContentRoot inside the hashed context, measured before the checks and re-verified after; check writes go to discarded scratch overlays; one tested_root source per mode. Build outputs come from a declared build stage whose products are captured and then examined read-only.
open_obligations.original_test: A legacy check writes a new file into the world tree: the file is absent from the promoted PRIME or the collapse refuses CANDIDATE_SNAPSHOT_CHANGED (the 1.9.1 control promotes it).

open_obligations.title: Report verdicts are parsed permissively and decided by TESTED Python (skipped, failing or regressed runs read as PASS)
open_obligations.target: A report verdict is PASS only if at least one testcase executed and none failed, errored or was skipped, and a benchmark regression is FAIL. The verdict is computed in SPARK from facts produced independently of Python (Report_Facts).
open_obligations.closure_required: Ship the M3 A3 strict, total parser with named FAIL reasons, then replace it as the authority with a SPARK parser (or proved count extractor) for the strict JUnit subset over the retained report bytes, feeding Report_Facts so Classify decides the status; the Python parser becomes diagnostic only.
open_obligations.original_test: JUnit tests=5 skipped=5 gives FAIL NO_TESTCASE_EXECUTED; a testcase with a failure child and zero suite counts gives FAIL; a benchmark with improved=False and exit 0 gives FAIL. gnatprove level 3 on the parser with 0 justified; G3 L2 corpus parity through the SPARK path.

open_obligations.title: Examiner imports are not confined to the staged bundle (PASS with unsatisfied imports admitted; candidate modules can run inside the private examiner)
open_obligations.target: No code from the candidate tree ever executes inside the examiner principal, and a PASS counts only when every import and read resolved inside the staged verifier bundle or the standard library; otherwise the check is EVALUATOR_INCOMPLETE. The evidence identifies every trusted input that influenced the verdict.
open_obligations.closure_required: Run examiners with -I -S and an audit hook (sys.addaudithook on import/open) that records the actual read/import set and refuses any module whose origin lies outside the stdlib and /run/worldline-verifiers (PRIVATE_EVALUATOR_BOUNDARY_FAILED). Let the policy declare the candidate modules under test (candidateModules); any other unsatisfied import makes the PASS EVALUATOR_INCOMPLETE. Bind the non-candidate read set into the executed-verifier identity.
open_obligations.original_test: An examiner importing 'util' (absent from the bundle, present in the candidate tree) inside a function and passing is not admissible; an examiner inserting the candidate path and importing from it gets PRIVATE_EVALUATOR_BOUNDARY_FAILED and an UNTRUSTED report; a declared module under test is still allowed.

open_obligations.title: An admitted private report can carry a verdict the candidate wrote
open_obligations.target: An admitted report's verdict cannot be supplied by the candidate; a report that carries bytes the candidate wrote is not admissible.
open_obligations.closure_required: Track report provenance: the examiner broker records every candidate output the examiner read, and admission refuses a report whose testcase or verdict content matches candidate-written bytes. Ship a verifier lint that flags examiners passing candidate files straight into the report.
open_obligations.original_test: An examiner that copies candidate junit.xml into /run/worldline-report produces an UNTRUSTED report and the check is not admissible.

open_obligations.title: candidate.run still starts candidate bytes under the worker's identity and broker
open_obligations.target: Candidate bytes never run under the worker principal; every candidate process runs as the candidate principal.
open_obligations.closure_required: Make candidate.run start as the candidate principal and deprecate worker-identity candidate runs; restrict worker executables to system binaries and staged verifier bytes, refusing executables taken from the candidate copy.
open_obligations.original_test: A worker told to exec a candidate-tree binary is refused; candidate.run's role observation shows candidate uid/gid 2.

open_obligations.title: Private-evaluator roles can create nested user namespaces, and the cgroup-escape claim is not extended to them
open_obligations.target: Examiner, worker and candidate have nested user-namespace creation disabled, as worlds and checks do (--disable-userns), and a private role provably cannot leave its cgroup budget.

open_obligations.title: Case copies and the frozen-tree copy are not atomic snapshots
open_obligations.target: A case copy or frozen copy equals one consistent state of its source, even under a deliberate racing writer.
open_obligations.closure_required: Copy only from a source nobody can write during the copy (freeze or revoke the writer's process group, hand over ownership, or copy from a filesystem snapshot), then verify content hashes of source and copy.
open_obligations.original_test: A racing writer that alters content and restores mtime/size during copy-in or copy-out causes a whole-run refusal.

open_obligations.title: Private-report boundary facts are bootstrap literals and self-reports, not observations
open_obligations.target: Report boundary facts (mount exclusivity, role identity) are observed independently of the bootstrap before a report is admitted.
open_obligations.closure_required: Have the supervisor observe mount exclusivity and role identity from /proc/<pid>/mountinfo and credentials instead of trusting bootstrap literals; refuse admission when observation and claim disagree.
open_obligations.original_test: A bootstrap claiming exclusivity while the report mount is shared is refused.

open_obligations.title: Legacy checks share one scratch overlay, so earlier checks can steer later examiners
open_obligations.target: Each required verdict depends only on the pre-check snapshot and its PRIME examiner.
open_obligations.closure_required: Give each required check a fresh overlay, as private checks already have; declare any preparation dependency explicitly and record its outputs as evidence.
open_obligations.original_test: Two legacy checks, the first writing a marker and the second passing only if the marker exists: on the new engine the second does not PASS.

open_obligations.title: Declared services run candidate code as the daemon account and could write live PRIME (A21)
open_obligations.target: Only the policy authority changes live PRIME; no candidate code can.
open_obligations.closure_required: Run services in a mount namespace where the live roots are absent or read-only, under a separate uid; refuse policies that declare services until that holds.
open_obligations.original_test: A service that writes <live PRIME>/.worldline.json fails with EACCES or EROFS and the requirement is unchanged.

open_obligations.title: Declared services can make the supersession placeholder write fail, so an older PASS keeps speaking
open_obligations.target: The candidate has no veto over supersession (M3 soundness-1).
open_obligations.closure_required: Stop a world's services before its revalidation starts; put service-writable storage on a separate size-capped filesystem or quota; persist a revalidation-requested marker in pre-reserved space and refuse prepare while a requested revalidation has no recorded head.

open_obligations.title: A candidate can plant a dormant judge in a non-primary root that takes over at the next primary switch (claim narrowed in M3 Decision 11)
open_obligations.target: The v2 claim: a candidate cannot plant a judge that takes over at the next primary switch. Neither a non-primary .worldline.json nor any examiner it names can be changed by a candidate and later adopted.

open_obligations.target: A FAIL under a requirement is terminal for that (world, requirement), and requesting an evaluation is a controlled capability, so re-running a flaky or host-dependent check cannot produce an authorizing PASS.
open_obligations.closure_required: Kernel input 'a completed FAIL exists for this content under this requirement' read from an authenticated append-only history, with Decide refusing when true; item 6b capabilities restrict who may request revalidation, with an owner-only retry capability that records its reason.
open_obligations.original_test: PASS->FAIL->PASS under one requirement is refused with a named decision; the owner retry path authorizes and leaves a receipt; a non-owner revalidation request is refused.

open_obligations.title: Every listed client holds full promotion and destruction authority, and nothing in the evidence records who asked
open_obligations.target: Collapse, return, transaction commit, abort, prune, revalidation requests, simulate and ghost enable are per-requester capabilities decided daemon-side (and for promotion, by the kernel). A commit's follow-on effects (starting PRIME's declared services, opening terminals and moving windows on the daemon account's desktop after a return) belong to the requester's capability, not free side effects, and a delegated socket fd confers nothing beyond its grant. Every receipt and causal event records the requester, hashed into the chain.
open_obligations.closure_required: Item 6b: a requester-capability input to Decide bound to the peer credential and the transaction, with a refusal code in its postcondition; bind each operation to a capability grant (Authority v1 issuer); make destructive operations owner-only; record the SO_PEERCRED uid in every receipt and causal event.
open_obligations.original_test: A listed client without capability is refused commit, abort of another's transaction, prune of another's worlds and ghost.enable at the daemon (not the CLI); a request from a different peer than the preparer is refused by the kernel; a client collapse receipt names the requester uid and the chain verifies.

open_obligations.title: A checkpoint return can restore an older, looser policy (exempt from the requirement pair)
open_obligations.target: No listed-client act changes the judge in force; restoring an older policy needs an owner capability that binds the requirement it adopts.
open_obligations.closure_required: Compute Resulting_Requirement for Checkpoint_Return too; Decide requires equality or an owner-only 'adopt' capability (item 6b) carrying the expected requirement hash, and records the adopted requirement.
open_obligations.original_test: A non-owner return to an older-policy checkpoint is refused REQUIREMENT_CHANGED; the owner with the adopt capability is AUTHORIZED and receipted; R-A1-9 same-policy returns are unchanged.

open_obligations.title: Newest-speaks does not survive a rollback: a superseded pre-upgrade PASS revives
open_obligations.target: A superseded evaluation never regains authority, including across an engine rollback.
open_obligations.closure_required: The rollback path, running under 1.10 before the swap, moves every census world into a state the older engine already refuses (from 1.7.3's existing refusals), or records the supersession in a form 1.7.3 honours.
open_obligations.original_test: R5's revival assertion flips: after rollback, prepare of the census world is refused under 1.7.3.

open_obligations.title: A checkpoint return checks that a world was once live, not that the restored bytes are that world's
open_obligations.target: A checkpoint return restores exactly the bytes checkpoint S had when displaced (S.components and content_id), witnessed by S's own committed receipt, and the kernel decides this.
open_obligations.closure_required: Add a kernel pair in Checkpoint_Return mode: the recorded return-point root against a recapture of the payload to be restored; run verify_content against S's recorded components and content_id; require the witnessing receipt to be the one whose afterRoot is S.
open_obligations.original_test: Replace S's payload with another historical live state with a consistent manifest: the return refuses (the 1.9.1 control restores it). Edit one byte of an archived prime-* payload with the Python check stubbed: the kernel refuses.

open_obligations.title: Re-application under finalization-only evidence is not bound to the bytes re-applied
open_obligations.target: Re-application re-applies only W's evaluated bytes: W's delta_hash and components are verified against the re-applied payload and manifests.
open_obligations.closure_required: Verify manifests and payload against W's recorded content_id and delta_hash before re-applying; refuse a mismatch.
open_obligations.original_test: After a consistent same-uid edit of W's payload and manifests, the return is refused.

open_obligations.title: Promotion mode, checkpoint witness and row resolution are decided by unproved Python over store fields and an ambiguous lookup
open_obligations.target: The promotion mode is derived from authenticated facts (the prepared transaction's typed mode), whether a return subject was ever live PRIME is decided by the proved Worldline.Ancestry over chained lineage records, and no alias can collide with an instance_id or content_id.
open_obligations.closure_required: Export and call Worldline.Ancestry over the chained lineage records; select Evaluation_Mode from the prepared transaction's typed mode, recomputed at commit and compared with the JSON; enforce reserved actors at write time; refuse aliases equal to any id and look up by id kind.
open_obligations.original_test: Synthetic never-live world with the Python walk stubbed to 'witnessed': the kernel refuses CHECKPOINT_UNWITNESSED. actor='worldline' on a once-live row, or a flipped JSON mode: refused. An alias equal to another world's id is refused at creation.

open_obligations.title: Prepare-to-commit change checks for the candidate payload are Python-only
open_obligations.target: Commit authorizes only if PRIME, the candidate payload and the record schema are what prepare saw, decided in the kernel.
open_obligations.closure_required: Add kernel pairs: prepared beforeRoot against the commit recapture and prepared candidateRoot against the commit recapture; pass the record schema version as a typed input Well_Formed checks.
open_obligations.original_test: Alter the candidate payload between prepare and commit with the Python compare disabled: the kernel refuses.

open_obligations.title: Pair producer independence is assumed: one value passed to both sides of an identity pair satisfies the proof
open_obligations.target: Every identity pair Decide compares is produced from two independent records, and a value copied to both sides (or a wrong digest stated on both) cannot reach AUTHORIZED; Resulting_Requirement is never computed from live PRIME.
open_obligations.closure_required: Hash each side under a per-pair, per-source domain tag and have Decide/Well_Formed require the two distinct source tags; or give the kernel the two source records and let it hash each side. Extend the static audit so no pair is assigned from one expression; compute Resulting in a separate producer from the staging bytes and compare.
open_obligations.original_test: For each pair in the 'Where each pair comes from' table, corrupt exactly one source record and assert the named *_MISMATCH; feed the same tagged value to both sides and assert refusal; a static-audit case fails when a pair is built from one variable; G5 mutation 'Resulting read from live PRIME' is killed by a kernel refusal.

open_obligations.title: The evaluation admission path from raw observations to Admissible is not proved end to end (unproved C decode, Python classification carry, Boolean roster)
open_obligations.target: Promotion admissibility is decided in SPARK from raw observations: every decode/validate step on the authorization path is proved (as Collapse_Wire.Decode is), and Decide recomputes roster completeness itself.
open_obligations.closure_required: An Evaluation_Wire SPARK unit (Decode + Classify_Wire) with Post: refused unless Well_Formed, otherwise exactly Classify/Admissible of Decode(R); a single SPARK Admit entry; Decide carries per-check classifications plus the declared roster and recomputes Roster_Complete (a conjunct of All_Hold). Delete the Python classification carry; add the units to REQUIRED_PROVED and CONTRACT_PINS; remove the item from the manifest's unproved boundary.
open_obligations.original_test: GNATprove level 3 with 0 justified; a forged-field corpus (Boolean exitCode, empty bundle, missing verdict, extra/omitted roster entry) is never admissible; a runtime double claiming a complete roster with one required check missing is refused EXECUTION_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE; the exhaustive evaluation oracle through the new entry shows 0 disagreements.

open_obligations.title: A stored report status is never re-derived from the retained report bytes (dropped from M3 A3)
open_obligations.target: The status that speaks at promotion is re-derived from the retained report bytes by proved or independently produced code, so a store rewrite of the status is refused.
open_obligations.closure_required: Re-derive the status from payloadB64 at classification with the SPARK parser of OB-007, or MAC (payload, status) with a key held outside the daemon uid; refuse on disagreement.
open_obligations.original_test: R-A3-4 flips to refused with a named decision: a stored PASS whose retained payload parses to FAIL is refused at promotion.

open_obligations.title: 'An ERROR head never authorizes' rests on a Python-written, unkeyed 'source' field (M3 Decision 15)
open_obligations.target: It is proved that an evaluation that did not complete never satisfies Roster_Complete.
open_obligations.closure_required: Give the kernel a completion fact it derives itself (a completion record the runner writes last, classified by Classify, with a Roster_Complete Post clause over it), or authenticate contexts as in OB-040.
open_obligations.original_test: In a lab store, forge source=revalidation on an ERROR head: prepare still refuses; the G5 mutation of the conjunct is killed by R-A6-11.

open_obligations.title: Revalidation reads PRIME three times without a generation guard and trusts a stored base manifest
open_obligations.target: A revalidation context states exactly the requirement and verifier bytes its checks ran under, from one generation-guarded read, and stored base manifests are verified with verify_content.
open_obligations.closure_required: Take one snapshot with a generation check before and after, and verify_content the base manifest.
open_obligations.original_test: A race harness changing the policy between the reads makes revalidation refuse REVALIDATION_INPUT_CHANGED.

open_obligations.title: The judge's execution identity (interpreter, tool and toolchain binaries, forwarded environment) is recorded by path only
open_obligations.target: Evidence is a statement about particular bytes under particular rules, including the interpreter, argv0 binaries and their libraries, sandbox and toolchain binaries and the forwarded environment; any change to them makes evidence stale.
open_obligations.closure_required: Hash the resolved interpreter and argv0 binaries (with ELF dependencies), the examiner toolchain mount, declared /usr tools and the forwarded environment into the execution half of the requirement, or run examiners in a pinned toolchain image whose hash is in the requirement.
open_obligations.original_test: Replace /usr/bin/python3 or bwrap bytes in a lab image: stored evidence becomes EVIDENCE_STALE with differences naming the binary.

open_obligations.title: Commit recomputes Resulting_Requirement from a staging location taken from the prepared record
open_obligations.target: Commit recomputes Resulting_Requirement from a location derived from the transaction id, never from JSON.
open_obligations.closure_required: Derive the staging paths from the transaction id and refuse any record whose path differs.
open_obligations.original_test: R-A1-4 variant: rewrite stagingPayload to a decoy inside the transaction directory; commit refuses.

open_obligations.title: Ownership (uid/gid) is not recorded, so chown/chgrp in live PRIME is neither measured nor part of content identity
open_obligations.target: Every change to live PRIME that no record accounts for is measured, ownership included, and content identity covers ownership; a receipt never states foreignWorldContamination NONE while an unmeasured change is present.
open_obligations.closure_required: Add uid and gid to manifest entries and the content root under a new domain tag (as T6 did), and compare them in the foreign-write measurement with FOREIGN_MANAGED_WRITE on mismatch. Owner is 1.10.0 because a domain-tag change stales all stored evidence and cannot ship in a patch.
open_obligations.original_test: chgrp a file in live PRIME with no watcher event: the next prepare refuses FOREIGN_MANAGED_WRITE and records unaccounted-write; a staged tree differing only in gid gives STAGED_UNTESTED; a mutant dropping uid/gid from the comparison fails.

open_obligations.title: Content roots and payload integrity omit behaviour-relevant metadata (modes, xattrs, ACLs, hard-link grouping, root-directory metadata, repository facts)
open_obligations.target: Two trees with the same content root behave the same, and payload integrity covers every field that can change behaviour; any exclusion is proven behaviour-neutral and stated in the kernel-facing spec.
open_obligations.closure_required: Extend the manifest, content root and verify_content to normalized modes, xattrs, ACLs, hard-link grouping, root-directory metadata and repository facts for repo roots, under a new domain tag (1.10.0, for the same reason as OB-037).
open_obligations.original_test: A staged tree differing only in root-directory mode or a hard-link pair gives STAGED_UNTESTED; a chmod-only or xattr-only change to a staged payload gives PAYLOAD_INTEGRITY_FAILED.

open_obligations.title: Nothing checks at decision time that the kernel answering Decide is the proved build (library selectable by environment)
open_obligations.target: Every Decide is answered by the exact proved kernel build named in a root-owned, signed proof manifest; a substituted library can neither authorize a promotion nor obtain a PROVED receipt.
open_obligations.closure_required: At prove time record the digest of the library built reproducibly from the pinned tree; sign {library sha256, proof-manifest digest, gnatprove run receipt} with a key held outside the daemon uid (vendored ATTEST Ed25519); at load and before every Decide hash the mapped library through its fd (or check an fs-verity digest) against the signed manifest; ignore WORLDLINE_CORE_LIB in deployed mode; refuse KERNEL_IDENTITY_MISMATCH; bind the digest into receipts.
open_obligations.original_test: Swap in a .so (or set WORLDLINE_CORE_LIB to one) whose Decide always authorizes, before start and after start: the daemon refuses at start and at the next Decide, and no receipt states PROVED. An unsigned or altered manifest is refused.

open_obligations.title: Kernel inputs read from the store and the prepared JSON are unauthenticated (same-uid forgery satisfies every pair)
open_obligations.target: Commit and recovery decide only on facts they recompute or on prepare-time facts, evaluation records, contexts, executed-verifier sets, history entries and epochs authenticated with a key a same-uid process cannot use; consistent forgery is detected and refused.
open_obligations.closure_required: Compare every prepare-time half with the DB row now; then have the producers (private evaluator, root broker, signer account) MAC or sign each prepared record, evaluation record, context and history entry with a key outside the daemon uid, hash-chain the history so deletions are detectable, verify before values reach the kernel, and remove the false 'signed' comment.
open_obligations.original_test: Between prepare and commit consistently edit testedRoot, rosterComplete, executedVerifiers, stagedRoot and the staging payload: TRANSACTION_RECORD_INVALID (1.9.1 control is COMMITTED). A forged set of PASS records, executed identity and context with consistent unkeyed digests is refused. Deleting a history entry is detected.

open_obligations.title: What is hashed and compared (manifests, canonical encoding, requirement/execution identities, report and resource admission, sandbox setup) is unproved Python
open_obligations.target: The values that reach the kernel are computed by proved code, or by an independent producer, from raw records: canonical encoding is injective and manifests, content roots and requirement identities are complete.
open_obligations.closure_required: Move canonical encoding and manifest/content-root/requirement-identity construction, execution-identity selection and report admission into SPARK units over raw entry records, with proved injectivity/field-coverage postconditions, so the kernel derives each identity instead of receiving it; until then run an independent second implementation as a differential oracle in assurance.
open_obligations.original_test: Each moved unit enters REQUIRED_PROVED with pinned contracts; a differential test over generated trees and policies where every single-field mutation changes the identity; Python-side mutation tests can no longer change an Authorized result.

open_obligations.title: The staged tree can change between its commit-time recapture and the exchange
open_obligations.target: The bytes exchanged into PRIME are exactly the bytes the kernel authorized and the receipt's afterRoot and PRIME row name.
open_obligations.closure_required: Seal the staging tree before the recapture (daemon-private uid ownership, read-only bind, immutable or fs-verity attribute), exchange from the sealed tree, and re-verify the content root after the exchange, rolling back on mismatch.
open_obligations.original_test: Fault injection writing into staging between recapture and exchange: commit refuses or rolls back, PRIME is unchanged, and in every run afterRoot equals the live root.

open_obligations.title: Reconcile and root removal change PRIME without a kernel decision
open_obligations.target: Whitepaper principle 1: nothing becomes real except through an authorized collapse; every PRIME generation change is a kernel-checked transition.
open_obligations.closure_required: Route reconcile and root removal through the one transition service as kernel transitions (Reconcile/Remove modes) that require a measured watcher state and record attribution (operator edit or foreign write) as typed input.
open_obligations.original_test: A reconcile of a foreign write goes through the kernel and carries its measurement; a reconcile with no watcher measurement is refused.

open_obligations.title: root.remove of the primary silently promotes remaining[0]
open_obligations.target: Every primary succession is explicit and receipted: root.remove of the primary refuses unless the successor is named, and the switch records the requirement it adopts.
open_obligations.closure_required: root.remove of the primary refuses with a named code unless the request names the successor and its expected requirement hash, and it emits a judge-change record (OB-045). Release-note it as a breaking change for scripts.
open_obligations.original_test: root.remove of the primary without a successor is refused; with a successor it is recorded with the adopted requirement hash.

open_obligations.title: No judge-change record and no mechanised, owner-authorized policy-change path (M3 Decision 6)
open_obligations.target: Every change to the requirement in force produces one ordered, receipted judge-change record (requirement before and after) through a mechanised owner-authorized path: live PRIME write, reconcile, restart resetting dirty, root.add/root.remove, engine or configuration change, checkpoint return.
open_obligations.closure_required: The transition service: every PRIME mutation goes through one owner-authorized service that computes Resulting_Requirement, checks the actor's capability and appends a signed judge-change event; direct live writes are refused, or detected and reported.
open_obligations.original_test: Each listed path emits exactly one judge-change record with correct before/after hashes; a direct live write is refused or reported with no record claimed.

open_obligations.title: Authority v1 enforcement exists only as installed labs; production promotions are not governed by it, and protected heads have no production owner
open_obligations.target: Production promotions pass through the composed Authority v1 transaction (intent gate, capability issuer with consumed use, live examiner evidence chain, resource ledger, Universe registry), and the capability, evidence and Universe protected heads are composed and owned by the production authority. Mediation is enforced by the OS, not by convention: the daemon account's Python cannot mutate live PRIME except through the protected actuator, every actuation is re-observed and bound to durable transaction evidence, and a bypass campaign on the production topology shows it (roadmap Phase 2 exit gate).
open_obligations.closure_required: The install-authority actuator design, then production integration of the composed transaction and heads under the root authority, with a drill and review.
open_obligations.original_test: In production, a promote without a gate admission or grant is refused, and the full denial campaign (rollback, deletion, forgery of each head) runs on the production topology. A direct-write campaign from the daemon account, the operator account and a client changes no live PRIME outside the actuator.
open_obligations.needs_operator: yes and password for the production topology change

open_obligations.title: Supervision facts come from journal scraping: a same-uid _COMM=systemd injection can forge SUPERVISED
open_obligations.target: Supervision facts (SUPERVISED, STOPPED, exit) come from an authenticated manager source that a same-uid process cannot forge and that does not depend on journal persistence.
open_obligations.closure_required: Read unit results from the systemd user manager over D-Bus (transient unit Result, ExecMainCode, ExecMainStatus), or match only journal fields a client cannot set (_PID of the manager, _SYSTEMD_USER_UNIT).
open_obligations.original_test: A lab injection of a forged _COMM=systemd entry leaves supervision INDETERMINATE; with a volatile journal a real run still reads SUPERVISED through D-Bus.

open_obligations.title: The remaining C entry glue (pointer dereference, exception handlers, file/byte hashing marshalling) is pinned by digest, not proved
open_obligations.target: The unproved C surface is minimal (null check, call, exception-to-255 mapping) and every data-handling path, including hashing marshalling, is proved.
open_obligations.closure_required: Move wl_hash_file/wl_hash_bytes read and length handling into SPARK with proved buffer bounds; leave C_API with only the null check, the call and the exception-to-255 mapping for every export.
open_obligations.original_test: Proof coverage of the new units; fuzzing of every exported C entry; a static-audit test that c_api.adb has no logic beyond the call pattern.

open_obligations.title: Recovery publishes PRIME without a kernel decision (unauthenticated markers; live capture for pre-1.9.0 records)
open_obligations.target: Every PRIME publication, including one completed by crash recovery, is authorized by a kernel decision recovery re-derives; recovery marks COMMITTED only after verifying that live/<key> resolves to the authorized staged payload and a durable one-shot authorization exists, otherwise it aborts or quarantines; an offline write is never folded into a collapse generation.
open_obligations.closure_required: Item 7: persist an authenticated AUTHORIZED record (durable one-shot authorization consumed exactly once); a SPARK recovery state machine that resolves the live mapping by kernel identity, recaptures and compares with the authorized staged root, re-runs Decide from integrity-protected decisionInputsAtCommit and finishes only on AUTHORIZED; for legacy records reconstruct and verify the staged root or quarantine TRANSACTION_RECORD_LEGACY.
open_obligations.original_test: Forge the live generation marker and the prepared mapping marker for a PREPARED transaction and restart: quarantine or abort with no receipt. Crash after the exchange with a hand-edited decisionInputsAtCommit: quarantine. A 1.8.0-format exchanged record plus an offline write: the published generation equals the recorded staged root or the transaction is quarantined. Crash injection at each commit step: no double commit and no commit without an unconsumed authorization.

open_obligations.title: Deleting or rewriting config.json silently resets policy to fail-open defaults
open_obligations.target: A missing or altered config never lowers protection: network, resource ceilings and anchor export default closed; the config is integrity-bound; operator edits are never overwritten.
open_obligations.closure_required: Fail-closed defaults, a root-owned integrity-bound config, compare-and-swap save, and owner-only ghost.enable (with OB-023).
open_obligations.original_test: Delete config.json and start: the daemon refuses or starts with closed defaults; ghost.enable from a client is refused.

open_obligations.title: Admission fails open when its ledger is deleted and misses work outside the gate
open_obligations.target: Admission is decided by a proved rule and fails closed: it refuses when its ledger is missing, observes under its lock, meters all work including checks, doctor --refresh and git inspection, and its reservations satisfy the proved invariants of OB-198 (conservation, parent/child containment, no double release, no running workload without an active reservation), with the resource epoch an input to Decide (roadmap-requirements.md:105, :108).
open_obligations.closure_required: Interim (WORLDLINE 1.9.8): refuse when the ledger is absent, observe inside the lock, attach reservations to transient units, meter doctor --refresh and git inspection. Closure (Phase 1 item 4): admission through OB-198's proved rule and resource epoch; later integrate the protected Authority v1 resource ledger (b7bcde9).
open_obligations.original_test: With the ledger deleted, admission refuses; doctor --refresh consumes a reservation. The OB-198 proof covers the admission path, and a Python double that admits everything is still refused by the kernel.

open_obligations.title: The client-mode boundary depends on unit, install and account integrity the daemon does not verify
open_obligations.target: The daemon refuses to serve clients when its unit, drop-ins, install tree or account are writable by a client.
open_obligations.closure_required: At start, check ownership and modes of the unit FragmentPath, its DropInPaths and the engine install tree against the client uids and group; refuse, and report in doctor.
open_obligations.original_test: A client-writable drop-in makes client mode refuse at start.

open_obligations.title: Disjointness of the client group and the daemon's group is only partly verified
open_obligations.target: No account is in both the client group and the daemon's group.
open_obligations.closure_required: Enumerate pwd.getpwall() for pw_gid == client_gid and check os.getgrouplist against the daemon gid; refuse client mode when enumeration is incomplete (non-enumerable NSS), or refuse all group-write bits in client-reachable content.
open_obligations.original_test: A fixture account with primary group = client group and supplementary daemon group gives INVALID_CLIENT_MODE at start.

open_obligations.title: The client-mode gate can stay open with no checking daemon, and store-lock ambiguity leaves it as it was
open_obligations.target: The data-directory gate is open only while a daemon that checked the content is running; any ambiguity (hard-linked lock, cannot tell, relative XDG path) closes it.
open_obligations.closure_required: An ExecStopPost= helper (runs even after SIGKILL) that chmods the data directory 0700; close the gate on every refusing start that can name its store; record the lock's dev/ino at creation, refuse nlink>1, and close the gate on ambiguity unless a daemon answers on the socket.
open_obligations.original_test: kill -9 the daemon: the data directory is 0700. A relative XDG config leaves the gate closed. A hard-linked lock is refused by name and the gate is closed.

open_obligations.title: The single-writer store lock can be defeated, and the store is opened and migrated before ownership checks
open_obligations.target: At most one daemon ever serves a store, and store ownership, type and schema are checked before any write.
open_obligations.closure_required: flock an object that cannot be unlinked from under the holder (the state directory's or database fd) and periodically verify the lock path's inode; open with O_NOFOLLOW and check fstat ownership before connecting, and migrate only after the checks.
open_obligations.original_test: Remove the lock file while daemon A runs and start daemon B with another runtime directory: B refuses DAEMON_ALREADY_RUNNING. A symlinked or foreign database is refused with its bytes unchanged.

open_obligations.title: Isolation binaries other than bubblewrap are not digest-pinned or attested
open_obligations.target: Every binary the private boundary relies on is digest-pinned in the run plan and re-checked before use.
open_obligations.closure_required: Pin digests of unshare, newuidmap, newgidmap, setpriv, python3 and the toolchain in the run plan; the bootstrap re-checks them as it does bubblewrap and refuses on mismatch.
open_obligations.original_test: Swap in a modified setpriv or unshare in a fixture: the run refuses before any role runs.

open_obligations.title: Subordinate IDs mapped to the worker and candidate roles are not checked for use by other host accounts
open_obligations.target: The host identities mapped to worker and candidate belong to no other account on the host.
open_obligations.closure_required: Before any role runs, read /etc/subuid, /etc/subgid and NSS passwd/group and refuse if any other account's uid/gid or subordinate range overlaps the IDs mapped to roles 1 and 2.
open_obligations.original_test: A host fixture with an account whose uid equals the worker's mapped host uid refuses the run by name.

open_obligations.title: Sandbox construction and isolation are Python-configured and never checked against a declared specification
open_obligations.target: The isolation boundary (what a world, check, examiner or worker can see and write) is checked against a declared specification on every build.
open_obligations.closure_required: A declarative sandbox specification (visible paths, rw/ro, sockets, namespaces); generate the bwrap argv from it in one audited place; run a mandatory in-sandbox census in assurance comparing the observed view with the spec.
open_obligations.original_test: An assurance step enumerates mounts and writable paths from inside an agent world, a check sandbox and a private examiner/worker and fails on any difference from the spec.

open_obligations.title: SHA-256 functional correctness is tested against vectors, not proved
open_obligations.target: Every digest equality Decide proves rests on a hash implementation proved to compute SHA-256 (functional postconditions, not only absence of runtime errors).
open_obligations.closure_required: Prove ATTEST SHA-256 against a functional FIPS 180-4 model in SPARK and pin that proof into the WORLDLINE proof manifest (vendoring per OB-175).
open_obligations.original_test: GNATprove of the functional contract; the published vectors retained as regression.

open_obligations.title: Authority v1 C12: a root caller with a fresh operation id can drive the broker directly
open_obligations.target: The broker commits only promotions admitted by the intent gate and bound to the gate-journaled operation and capability, whatever the caller's uid.
open_obligations.closure_required: The broker requires a gate-signed admission token (key held by the gate principal) bound to operation_id, capability and Universe head, or a SPARK court verifying the gate journal entry before prepare.
open_obligations.original_test: A root promote with a fresh operation_id and no gate admission is refused; the gate-admitted positive control commits.

open_obligations.title: Authority v1 R1/C2: a promote can commit under a revoked grant
open_obligations.target: No promotion commits under a revoked grant; the broker rechecks the capability under its own lock before commit, and a queued recover cannot resume a promote the operator stopped.
open_obligations.closure_required: The broker rechecks with the issuer under its own lock at every transition that can reach commit; recover carries the grant epoch and refuses a stale one.
open_obligations.original_test: Revoke during a long in-flight promote: refused before commit. A queued recover after the gate stops and the grant is revoked: refused.

open_obligations.title: Capability ID uniqueness is a value-only predicate over caller-supplied ancestry
open_obligations.target: Capability ID uniqueness is enforced against the custody registry, with the C ABI, adapter and replay inside the proof boundary.
open_obligations.closure_required: Derive the ancestry from the root-owned anchored registry, never from the caller.
open_obligations.original_test: Fabricated, consistent ancestry with a reused ID is refused.

open_obligations.title: Authority v1 protected commit veto does not authenticate all daemon facts
